result:
The file-level audit warnings are fixed and typecheck still passes. The audit still reports two dependency advisories (`katex` and `source-map-js`) that come from `bun.lock`, not from this change. I left them alone because upgrading packages is outside this task.

Changes in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`:
- **`destroy`** now calls `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` before deleting. This was a real gap: the policy's delete rule was never enforced, so any signed-in user could delete any post.
- **`store`** now uses `Post.create(data, { set: { authorId: author.id } })` instead of `forceCreate({ ...data, authorId })`, so the request data goes through fillable.
- **`keepRevision`** now uses `PostRevision.create` instead of a force write.

In `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`, I added `fillable: ['postId', 'title', 'excerpt', 'body']` to clear the mass-assignment warning on the new model. I did not add any `guren-audit-ignore` exceptions.
